CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR JULY 11, 2022 AT 4:30 P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE
SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of
the public may provide live public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to
the start of public comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker Card Help Line : If
a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card, please
call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the posted
start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Your phone call to the City Council
meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By
staying on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting,
you are agreeing to have your phone call recorded.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may
submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be
forwarded to the City Council prior to the start of the meeting, posted online,
and made part of the legislative record for the item.

4:30 P.M. TENDRÁ LUGAR ÚNICAMENTE POR VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente
por medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la
siguiente manera:
1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del
público pueden hacer comentarios públicos en vivo presentando una tarjeta de
oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artículo que se está tratando
en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la
agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Línea
de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública :
Si un orador de comentario
p úblico
necesita asistencia para completar su tarjeta, puede llamar
a la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al
(626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30
minutos antes del inicio de la reunión.
Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual
a la
h ora
de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico o por
teléfono. Debe usar el
mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la reunión
virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo
Municipal se grabará como parte de la reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al
permanecer en la línea y hacer
comentarios públicos durante la
reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que se grabe su llamada
telefónica.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunión: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del público
pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud antes del inicio de
la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La
correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el
artículo.

   Mayor Gordo read a statement and provided an overview of the staff

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring July 2022 as "Parks
  Make Life Better Month," in the City of Pasadena. Brenda Harvey-
  Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services,
  received the proclamation, provided information on the Department's
  programs supporting the community, and expressed appreciation to
  the Mayor, City Council and the community for the recognition.

  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory of
  Theodore "John" Stacks Jr., a fixture at the intersection of Pasadena
  Avenue and Del Mar Boulevard for decades. Mayor Gordo
  recognized Mr. Stacks for his work ethic and tenacity to overcome the
  challenges in his life, his kindness and positivity with strangers and
  friends alike, and how he helped make the community a better place.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Michael Williams, Pasadena resident, advocated for the termination
MATIERS NOT ON THE  of Pasadena Police Officers Dumaguindin and Serrano involved in
AGENDA  the shooting of Anthony McClain, advocated for holding the
  Pasadena Police Officers accountable, and urged the City Council to
  take action on this matter.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquire related to the
  Anthony McClain administrative review, Interim City Manager shared
  information on the administrative review process, noting that it is
  expected to conclude by the end of July.

  Ryan Bell, representing Pasadena Tenants Union, expressed
  concerns and spoke on dozens of no-fault evictions occurring across
  the City violating a Los Angeles County resolution, and urged the City
  to help circulate information on tenants' rights and referred the
  community to https://dcba.lacounty.gov/noevictions/ for more
  information.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton concerns related to the
  evictions of tenants in Pasadena, Interim City Manager Kurtz stated
  the City Council adopted an ordinance ending the City's Moratorium
  on evictions effective June 30, 2022, and highlighted that the City has

Council Minutes  2  07/11/2022
   set aside $2.5 million dollars for rental assistance to low-income
  residents covering non-payment and back rent rental assistance. The
  City Manager noted that the information is posted on the City of
  Pasadena website and questions related to the program may be
  directed to the City Manager's Office and the Housing Department.

  City Attorney Bagneris noted that tenants can seek assistance at the
  Housing Rights Center with respect to help with eviction notices.

  Councilmember Hampton asked the Public Information Office (PIO)
  to circulate the information to the community.

  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident, welcomed the new City Manager,
  and spoke on matters related to the shooting of Anthony McClain,
  stating that the change in City leadership should focus on resolving
  this matter as requested by the community.

  Jonathan Fuhrman, Pasadena resident, spoke on issues of housing
  density and housing growth in Pasadena, advocating for increased
  allowable density, heights, reduced required parking, helping
  developers to produce new housing units; spoke in opposition to the
  revised South Fair Oaks Specific Plan; and followed up on comments
  by Mr. Bell that the tenants being evicted have continued to pay their
  rent yet are being evicted on the pretext that the landlords wish to
  upgrade the rental units.

  Hiram Cormier Jr., Los Angeles resident, advocated for justice for
  Anthony McClain and other victims of officer-involved shootings, and
  urged the new City Manager to fire the Police Officers involved in
  shooting residents.

  Geoffrey Baum,  representing West Pasadena Residents'
  Association, welcomed the new City Manager Judge Marquez,
  expressed thanks and appreciation to Cynthia Kurtz for her work and
  dedication as Interim City Manager, and spoke in support of finding
  new revenue enhancement measures for the Rose Bowl, while
  advocating for a robust process where neighbors have the
  opportunity to provide their opinions, guidance, and support.

  Marie Perez, Pasadena resident, expressed her concerns
  surrounding a 60-day eviction notice she received on July 1, 2022, a
  10% rent increase that recently went into effect, the use of
  renovations and repairs to justify rent increases and evictions, stating
  that these changes result in housing that only the rich can afford.

  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community Happen,
  express her thanks and appreciation to City for breaking ground on
  the 69 unit affordable housing project for homeless seniors,
  acknowledged the City Council for being a model for many other cities
  and expressed her excitement for the new City Manager.

Council Minutes  3  07/11/2022
   Heavenly Hughes, representing My TRIBE Rise, echoed all the
  comments from previous speakers, and urged the new City Manager
  to bring healing to the community by looking closely into community
  claims of corruption and police brutality occurring in Pasadena; and
  thanked the City for recognizing the Juneteenth holiday.

  Adrianna Bautista, representing BLM Dena, advocated for the
  termination of Pasadena Police Officers Dumaguindin and Duncan
  involved in the shooting of Anthony McClain, and spoke on the District
  Attorney's (DA) report of the incident, stating she has requested the
  release of the Police body-worn camera footage of the shooting of
  Anthony McClain.

  responded to questions.

  requirements related to density, that a phased approach will continue
  to support housing opportunities with approximately 950 residential
  units and will provide the City Council with the latitude to revisit the
  South Fair Oaks Specific Plan proposed densities as further
  development involving residential housing occurs over time within the

  Plan update, requesting that staff further review the City's

  corridor/specific plan development production goal, which would help

  the City Council on the matter.

  Fuentes responded to questions related to inclusionary housing,
  noting that state law would require the City to do a Nexus Study on
  the return on investment and impacts.

  requirements, stating the "flexibility" should not defeat the intended
  functions of paseos; and advocated to implement the Complete Street

  to the City Council on the plan to implement a multimodal program on
  South Raymond; and requested incorporating language prioritizing

  Specific Plan.

  Housing Ordinance can vary in percentage by area/specific plan.

  questions regarding the process for amending the Specific Plan once
  approved, stating that the Specific Plan is a planning document that
  sets development parameters and policies, but does not "run with the
  land" and can be amended. She noted that the set density (which
  cannot be decreased) is constrained by state law; and stated that
  projects that comply with the specific plan parameters are by-right
  until such time as a project seeks a discretionary action where the
  approval would allow the project to exceed the set parameters.
